newsitem.title: UKRAINE: ITUR telecoms cable link to open under Black Sea.
newsitem.headline: ITUR telecoms cable link to open under Black Sea.

text.p: Italy, Turkey, Ukraine and Russia said on Thursday they would form a new link in the world's telephone cable network when their $155-million "ITUR" cable opened on November 1.
The 3,500-km (2,200-mile) fibre-optic cable runs under the Black Sea and the Mediterranean from Novorossiisk in Russia and Odessa in Ukraine, to Istanbul and Palermo.
"This will alow clear connections between Europe, South America, Canada and the United States," Ukraine's Communications Minister Dmytro Khudoliy said.

The four countries' communications ministers announced the opening by video link-up at simultaneous inauguration ceremonies, using the "ITUR" cable in public for the first time before its goes into service on Friday.
They ended the video-conference with a flourish, standing up and extending their hands in a virtual, one-sided handshake.
Telephone systems in former Soviet republics like Ukraine and Russia are outdated, long-distance connections are hard to make and lines are crackly.

Expensive satellite links have supported most of Ukraine's international connections since independence in 1991. "International and intercity rates will go down because of ITUR," said Georhiy Butenko, president of Ukrtelekom, Ukraine's telecommunications company.
ITUR will connect the countries to cables leading to Africa, and western European cables leading to North and South America.
Ukrtelekom will own 19.5 percent of the cable, its portion of the project largely financed by a credit from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).
The countries agreed to undertake the project in 1992 and subcontractors included France's Alcatel Submarcom, AT&T of the United States and Italy's Maristel.
Ukraine also announced a 975-km (600-mile) fibre-optic land link from Odessa to Kiev, to be completed this year, which will improve connections to Belarus, Russia, Poland and western Europe.
